transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

The things that used to mean everything to me—my garden, my quilts, my walks—don’t matter anymore, and I can’t make myself care about any of it. I feel like I’ve just lost all interest in the world, which is why my daughter and my pastor insisted I come talk to you.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling this low in the past?

These feelings have been hanging over me for well over a year now, about a year and five months since my sister passed away. I have never experienced anything like this before in my life, as I used to be very active and involved in my community.
Since these feelings began a year and five months ago, have there been any periods of a few weeks or more where you felt like your old self, or has this low mood been present almost every single day?

This heavy, joyless mood has been with me almost constantly, and I haven't felt like my old self at all. There was a brief spell last fall where I wasn't crying as much and my mood felt a bit more neutral, but I still didn't feel normal because I was still hearing my sister's voice and worrying about those church ladies watching me.

You mentioned that this is the first time you have felt this way; to be absolutely sure, have you ever experienced a distinct period of depression lasting several weeks or more at any point earlier in your life, even if it was many years ago?
No, I have never experienced a period of depression like this before in my life. I was always quite active and lively, keeping busy with my church and friends, until my sister passed away.

When you hear your sister's voice or worry about the women from church watching you, do you feel like these are real experiences that are actually happening, or do you sometimes wonder if they might just be in your head?

They feel completely real to me, and I am convinced those church ladies are actually watching me and talking behind my back, no matter what my daughter says. When I hear my sister, even though I know she is gone, her voice is so clear in the quiet house that it just doesn't feel like it's my imagination.

However, the presence of persistent, fixed delusional beliefs (paranoia regarding church members) and auditory hallucinations that she perceives as real, occurring in the context of a severe depressive episode, strongly points toward the presence of psychotic features. F32.2 is excluded because the clinical presentation now explicitly includes psychotic symptoms, making F32.3 the more accurate diagnosis.
